To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cats fed scFOS, or GOS, or scFOS +GOS diets had greater fecal Bifido bacteria, lower fecal pH, greater fecal butyrate, valerate, total short-chain fatty acids, and total branched chain fatty acids concentrations, and lower fecal ammonia, 4- methylphenol, indoles, and total fecal biogenic aminess.

supplementation of healthy adult cats with 0.5 g/kg BW/day of either scFOS or GOS or their combination resulted in a prebiotically positive effect on fecal microbial ecology and fecal metabolite production.

cats fed a diet supplemented with 0.5 % scFOS +0.5 % GOS had greater apparent total tract CP digestibilities and concentrations of fecal Bifodobacterium spp., butyrate, valerate, and total branched chain fatty acids than cats fed the control, 0.50 % scFOS or 0.50% GOS diets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of prebiotics on the health of cats.
the effects of scFOS and/or GOS on nutrient digestibility and fecal fermentative end products in healthy adult cats.
the effect of prebiotic supplementation on nutrient digestibilities, fecal metabolites, and large bowel microbiome of cats fed a commercial diet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of scFOS and galactooligo-saccharides may be beneficial for cats.
scFOS +GOS supplementation may be an effective prebiotic strategy in healthy adult cats.
the combination of scFOS and galactooligoscacharides is more effective than either alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
scFOS, and to a lesser extent GOS, have the potential to improve the health of cats by altering the microbial ecology of their gastrointestinal tract and the metabolites that they produce.
scFOS, and especially scFOS +GOS, are prebiotics in cats.

scFOS +GOS supplementation to cat diets may improve the health of the large bowel microbiota, but the effect is not strong enough to affect nutrient digestibility, blood leukocytes, or fecal protein catabolite concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cats can benefit from prebiotics, but that the effects are not necessarily additive when the prebiotics are used together.
cats are capable of responding to these types of prebiotics in a manner similar to what we have observed in other species.
the combination of scFOS and galactooligo-saccharide supplementation is more effective in improving some indices of gut health than either supplement alone.
